what: the five crude fixes of the gap register's --flip-check, each applied to a copy of the extractor and run through the stub harness, the property test (seed 1109, 5000 pages) and the real-browser fixture without its controls. The fixes are crude: the register notices them, and these runs say what the other tests make of them. None is a proposed final fix. Fix 5 was changed in round 7 (it now drops the bound in both places where it sits) and all its lines were rerun; fix 1 had not been run on the fixture and was in round 7. Fix 2 was reduced to its filter half in round 9, because its other half (a Unicode word boundary) stops scrubbing a name that touches a non-ASCII letter, and was rerun on all three tests. The over-masking audit of the property test never calls the extractor, so it is not a result of these runs.

fixes.name: text mask: NFKC fold, and any run of 7 or more digits with separators or an extension is a phone
fixes.harness: FAIL: the check "text outside buttons: emails and phone-like numbers are masked in headings, tabs, columns, labels and inputs" (the heading Report 2026-10-01, which must survive, becomes Report <phone>)
fixes.property: FAIL: its phone gap no longer reaches the output on any page (0 of 2113, XPASS, which fails the run by design); no other failure
fixes.fixture: FAIL only through the expected-failure rule: all 59 contract runs PASS, and the phone gap turns XPASS in 43 gap checks (88 XFAIL), which fails the run by design

fixes.name: scrub: keep values with a letter in any script or 4 or more digits (the word boundary is left as it is)
contact links: any scheme other than http and https, and the wa.me and api.whatsapp.com hosts
title: an em dash, a middle dot and a colon also separate the name from the product
person link: any id after /user/ or /people/, not only 8 or more characters (in the person test and in the path mask)

not_run: the fixture with its controls on any fix, the property test on other seeds, and any real tenant
